approach.method_basis: The Parent grows a persistent tree of molecular graph edits and buys newly reached frontier molecules directly. Each accepted return updates the completed count, sum, maximum and pending ledger along its actual route. Before the first promotion and below the roots, structurally similar eligible siblings share peak values and exploration density. After a strict accepted improvement, search restarts from the current incumbent and the incumbent preceding that feedback batch, in that order, with their original accepted receipts as cached contexts. These two roots now compete using their own best accepted return, while completed and pending exploration counts are still shared through molecular similarity.
approach.novelty: Remove only pending-work borrowing between the promoted roots. Keep each root own peak value and shared completed density, but count only that root own unresolved purchases in its exploration denominator. This tests whether pending work on the other origin discourages useful exploration when value credit is already local. The earlier value-only change and the joint value-and-density removal do not identify this pending consumer. The parallel sibling removes completed-density borrowing instead; the earlier pending-only experiment intervened deeper on a different single-root host. This test preserves those results and measures one conditional contribution.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is continued cross-origin exploration discouragement on the own-value dual-root Parent n-fc3b91c9623a, whose value-only removal improved full endpoints but weakened late conversion. Its complete Search mean is 0.5001487124432433 (population SD 0.01368931088288767), versus 0.4809700595412967 for n-b13ef5ae4ba8: +0.019178652901946685. Full incumbent-increment mass is 4.37484902101401 over 4350 paid optimizer observations, but late mass is 0.8438973049856529 over 2175, below the previous 0.8656010443094923. It remains 0.1068816037678877 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. Independent archived-row reconstruction in policy/scratch/r0058-02-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen cited per-cell audits reproduces D/P/B, the own-M root consumer, initial/deeper shared consumers, exact winners and actual paid-route joins with zero mismatches. On the Parent actual states, replacing only D+P by D+O changes 5141/7484 promoted-root bonuses and 1806/3742 choices in 14/15 cells; 1741/4350 actual paid paths, including 908/2175 late paths, traverse changed positions. There are 65 changed but unpaid choices; 1791 switches are current-to-preceding and 15 reverse. The never-promoted median_2 seed-0 cell is retained. These passive alternatives have no purchased outcomes. The exposed joint removal n-51af92d7316d and value-only Parent cannot be subtracted to infer pending contribution. The deeper pending removal n-6a1ce58741d7 lost 0.041186024313750014 on its different host, warning that pending sharing can be useful under different retained values and boundaries.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse search-policy-r58-conditional-credit-and-optimality-probability and its recorded queries; no fresh literature query was issued for this plan. Implement only the frozen root pending-density removal on the own-value dual-root host. WU-UCT supplies background separation of completed and unresolved work, but neither its setting nor deeper sharing establishes this conditional contribution. RAVE blending and other reviewed methods are deferred. The experiment can identify only the scoped complete Search-panel sign, with exposure and full/late conversion reported separately.

Independent reconstruction of the actual own-value Parent source, selection rows and paid-route joins establishes natural exposure for the D+O consumer. The Parent full/late discrepancy, unresolved joint-removal contrast and condition-mismatched deeper pending counterexample motivate isolating this remaining dependency. No source method, external model/package, RAVE blend or new WU-UCT mechanism is adopted; actual pending accounting is inherited.

hypothesis: Within m-eca1b7eb5895, remove only off-diagonal pending-density consumption at selections satisfying episode > 0 and parent_id == 0 on code Parent n-fc3b91c9623a. With K the inherited eligible-sibling count-Tanimoto kernel, leave D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j and P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j computed and recorded unchanged. The active root started quantity becomes D_i+O_i rather than D_i+P_i, so only sum_{j!=i} K_ij*O_j is omitted from the exploration denominator and zero-start priority. Active exploitation remains M_i if N_i>0, else inherited neutral 0.5; active bonus is 0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D_i+O_i)) when started>0 and the existing None/priority convention when zero. Earliest occurrence wins ties. Actual own pending O_i and the parent pending numerator are retained. The causal activation claim is that naturally nonzero cross-origin pending support ceases to suppress these bonuses, producing different root choices that reach actual paid descendants; any score consequence is a separate measured hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Removing shared pending density changed paid choices but lost 0.04013 mean score
finding_summary.insights: Shared pending density has a positive conditional contribution when promoted roots already use their own accepted-return peaks and retain shared completed density. Removing it almost always redirects a changed choice from the current origin toward the preceding origin; realized preceding-origin purchases rise from 785 to 1,481, while current-origin purchases fall from 2,795 to 2,099. The result rules out score preservation for this frozen intervention, while leaving the broader tree approach and interactions with completed density open. It does not overturn the earlier benefit of removing shared root values: the two consumers have different conditional roles. The loss is concentrated unevenly across seeds, especially the first docking run, so neither generalization nor per-choice mediation is established. Methodologically, broader graph variety still fails to ensure useful chemical conversion. Typed scaffold unions increase from 1,684 to 1,744, yet the paid stream still contains 314 molecules below six heavy atoms and 287 above fifty, with both tails also present in the Parent. Molecular assessment finds useful intact aromatic/amine and aromatic/carbonyl combinations mixed with core-deleted fragments, repeated large cores and difficult bond or ring contexts. This supports a limitation in the proposal operator’s ability to change topology while preserving useful connected chemical environments, rather than literal scaffold collapse. A proposal operator with coherent functional-substructure edits and bond/ring-context awareness is the relevant missing kind of capability; this panel does not establish its score benefit. Candidate-exclusive timing, precise late timing, measured RNG invariance and independently trusted task-safety evidence remain unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The intended removal executed faithfully. It increased 6,068 exploration bonuses and indices and changed 1,269 of 3,830 promoted-root choices. Those changes reached 1,201 of 4,350 paid optimizer molecules, including 722 of 2,175 late purchases; 68 changed routes were abandoned. Fourteen task/seed cells were exposed. The never-promoted median task at seed 0 remained unexposed and unchanged. No selector, backup, pending-accounting or preserved-law violation was found. Mean score fell from 0.5001487124432433 to 0.46001796961200997, a paired loss of 0.04013074283123336: seven cells improved, seven worsened and one tied. Full incumbent-improvement mass fell from 4.37484902101401 to 3.772887878545513 over all 4,350 purchases; late mass fell from 0.8438973049856529 to 0.4888364972281913, with 30 strict improvements instead of 38. The registered score-preservation prediction is refuted. The separate formal Anchor mean remains 0.607030316211131, and its required improvement of 0.002 is not reached.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analogues and heteroatom cages, with persistent fragment tails and questionable bond chemistry
molecular.overall_character: This is an assessment of n-0fdf8aec31a2 against code Parent n-fc3b91c9623a, using the complete frozen Search panel at profile epoch 1, batch size 10. The request marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete for seeds 0, 1 and 2; all task trajectories are present and none is omitted. No additional historical node or formal Anchor chemistry comparison was read or inferred. The comparison is descriptive, with no mechanism-activation or component-attribution claim. All numerical chemistry summaries below are derived from accepted optimizer trajectory records; rejected suggestions and unpurchased structures are not represented. Initial observations are separate, and a last-proposed molecule is not the final incumbent. The 4350 paid optimizer molecules have median 26 heavy atoms, range 1 to 120; 314 contain fewer than 6 heavy atoms and 287 exceed 50. The late window, optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 within each cell, has 2175 molecules, median 26 heavy atoms, with 177 below 6 and 181 above 50. Parent full/late small-fragment counts are 306/143 and oversized counts 289/179. These tails coexist with ordinary aromatic amides, lactams, ethers, esters, phenols, nitriles and aliphatic amines. The digest ring-closure rates span 0.8644 to 0.9448 and aromatic-presence rates 0.5908 to 0.8793; these are SMILES-level indicators, not ring counts or fractions of atoms. RDKit gives 1744 nonempty typed and 1280 generic Murcko scaffold unions for the Child full panel, and 1008/760 late; the Parent has 1684/1188 full and 972/724 late. Thus broad structural diversity is real at the graph level, but some of it consists of fragmentation, irregular annulation and expansion. Radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto, excluding molecules below 6 heavy atoms and comparing only within the same task, seed and window, gives Child pair-weighted means 0.20115158041887574 over 541653 pairs full and 0.24419064917092126 over 132483 pairs late. Parent values are 0.20202255305312947 over 543335 pairs and 0.2532065461147983 over 136877 pairs. These are descriptive structure similarities, not the selector kernel and not evidence that broader chemistry improves utility. There are 296 Child molecules with O–O bonds and 496 with O–F bonds. Nitrogen–nitrogen and nitrogen–oxygen bonds also occur, but their presence alone is not a blanket liability. All digest stereocentre-token and charge-token rates are zero; RDKit identifies potentially unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2583 Child proposals. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of basicity, and unspecified stereochemistry does not establish an impossible molecule. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed: conventional aromatic analogues are present alongside peroxide-bearing derivatives, unusual fused or bridged cages, and heavily concatenated structures. No synthetic route, conformational feasibility, stability, affinity or drug-exposure measurement was supplied. No absent named pharmacophore is inferred from an objective title. Missing features below mean structures or structural control underrepresented relative to observed higher-scoring molecules, not a supplied answer to an unseen target. Provenance: policy/requests/r0058-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-3fa8fc7e0c9acd7c.json and policy/scratch/r0058-02-improve-L01-molecular/panel-audit.json. The latter lists every per-cell audit, underlying file and SHA-256. Child authority remains the original slot-2 staging trajectories explicitly listed in that frozen request; byte-identical scratch snapshots preserve their absolute source identity and hashes, and do not claim published archive status. Parent inputs are the published Search trajectories. Every input existed and was read. Origin/exposure-stratified chemistry, candidate timing, measured RNG invariance and trusted task-safety measurements are not established by this molecular audit.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer emits mainly substituted indoles, aryl amides and annulated nitrogen-containing lactams, with methoxy, methyl and aryl halogen decorations. The paid population has median 24 heavy atoms, range 1 to 64, with 81 molecules below 6 and 12 above 50. The best seed-0 molecule is a 24-heavy-atom, 4-ring annulated lactam attached to a fluorophenyl group; seed 1 retains a more conventional indole carboxanilide, and seed 2 reaches an indole/furan-like fused system bearing a pyridylamino substituent. These compact aromatic families look more synthetically interpretable than the later nitrogen/sulfur appendages and fragments. The Parent also emits compact indole-derived carbonyl aromatics, so neither generation lacks rings or carbonyl chemistry. Its best seed-1 and seed-2 examples are carbonyl-substituted indoles rather than the Child fused heteroaromatic endpoint families. Some annulations and nitrogen/sulfur substitutions introduce less conventional bond contexts without a corresponding demonstrated synthetic route.

The seed-0 hydrazone-like fused compound scores 0.3797978158599693 and the seed-2 amino bicyclic compound 0.19559268063469384. A 75-heavy-atom concatenation of ester, aromatic and nitrogen-rich units scores zero. A late compact hydrazine-bearing cage scores 2.5628672858791327e-12, so compactness alone is insufficient. The observed gradient distinguishes particular compact heteroatom/substituent arrangements from both overgrowth and other compact arrangements; it does not prove that cage strain or unusual bonds are necessary. Parent best scores are 0.36986596080763057, 0.4682757034117735 and 0.3078278090759092 in different heterocyclic families. No known-drug structure is used to prescribe missing chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-0fdf8aec31a2, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 at epoch 1 and batch 10: the audited 4350 paid proposals contain 314 structures below 6 heavy atoms and 287 above 50; the late 2175 contain 177 and 181 respectively. Parent n-fc3b91c9623a also shows both tails. This is an observed output limitation on this host, not evidence attributing fragmentation or growth to the changed selector.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve molecular scale while changing a useful connected core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo edits that preserve connected functional substructures while allowing deliberate changes in size and topology. Use only current-session feedback to discover useful scale; the audit thresholds describe tails and are not universal size cutoffs or objective-specific instructions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-0fdf8aec31a2 under the same frozen Search conditions: 296 paid molecules contain O–O bonds and 496 contain O–F bonds, and some strongest observed structures carry these motifs or densely bridged heteroatom cages. Parent n-fc3b91c9623a also contains such chemistry. These are structural observations; no synthesis, stability or geometry experiment was supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid graph diversity is not consistently accompanied by credible bond context and synthetic tractability.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide general bond-context and ring-geometry awareness during de novo construction so that decorated scaffolds can be explored through chemically interpretable alternatives. Do not equate every N–N or N–O bond with a defect, and do not assume that removing a liability must improve the oracle score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-0fdf8aec31a2, the same complete Search panel: strong aromatic amine combinations coexist with weak amine-only fragments; organized aromatic/carbonyl heterocycles coexist with weak core-deleted fragments and oversized repetitions. Full-panel typed/generic scaffold unions are 1744/1280, so the limitation is not literal absence of topology diversity. These within-session chemistry/score associations are not component attribution or a portable target pharmacophore.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful combinations of functional groups when it changes scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable coherent rearrangement and redecoration of intact chemical environments rather than relying solely on atom-count changes or nominal scaffold novelty. Let the current session identify which combinations matter, retain every source condition, and do not hard-code one task family or carry labels between sessions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-0fdf8aec31a2 under the same frozen Search conditions: every task digest has stereocentre-token rate 0.0, while RDKit identifies potentially unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2583 paid proposals, including densely bridged structures. This establishes a representation gap, not an experimentally measured stereochemical defect or a demonstrated source of score loss.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical definition is absent even when generated graphs contain potentially stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemically explicit, geometrically credible variants available through task-agnostic de novo construction where the graph warrants them. Their value must be learned from authorized current-session observations; the present evidence does not establish that a particular stereoisomer or charge state is rewarded.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
